purpose: Define rollback as an explicit recovery migration to a known compatible prior state, with data-loss checks, snapshot/revision evidence and no assumption that every forward migration is reversible.

topics.purpose: Define rollback as an explicit recovery migration to a known compatible prior state, with data-loss checks, snapshot/revision evidence and no assumption that every forward migration is reversible.

semantics.reversible_rule: Migration explicitly declares reversible, conditionally_reversible or irreversible.
semantics.snapshot_rule: Rollback requirements may include exact pre-migration snapshot/checkpoint.
semantics.reverse_rule: Reverse transformation is an explicit migration operation/profile.
semantics.loss_rule: Potential data loss or non-representable target-version data is detected and surfaced before rollback.
semantics.conflict_rule: Writes made after cutover are considered explicitly during rollback planning.
semantics.atomic_rule: Rollback accepted-state transition follows explicit transaction/restore semantics.
semantics.history_rule: Forward migration and rollback evidence remain preserved.

invariants.rule: Schema evolution is an explicit versioned migration between exact schema identities/versions with validated compatibility and data transformation provenance; runtime/file order never silently changes active data meaning.

references.purpose: Rollback can anchor exact pre-migration state.
Recovery replacement obeys explicit restore boundary.
